
In younger
palms, the stem is covered with narrow, triangular leaf bases of fallen
or pruned leaves. With age, multiple stems are formed (unless suckering
shoots are pruned); leaf scars spiraling, prominent raised knobs.

The large greenish or bluish gray pinnate leaves
are typically 18-20 ft (5.5-6.1 m) long by 2 ft (0.6 m) wide. Leaflets
are 1-2 ft
(0.3-0.6 m) long and arranged in V-shape ranks that run the length of
the leaf stem. Leaflets near the base are modified into sharp 3-4 in
(7.6-10.2 cm) spines. [1](https://www.growables.org/information/TropicalFruit/PalmPhoenixDactilifera.htm#Bibliography)
